extracted.subtask_description: A multi-item Associated Press news collection: international and domestic dispatches from the wire (civil defense test, armistice agreements, legal/regulatory board decisions, foreign-aid stats, political leadership changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Survival kit contents and use
rubrics_metrics.description: The family-tested civilian-defense survival kit recommendations: "THE KITS SHOULD CONTAIN MORE MEAT AND SOUP, MORE INSTANT COFFEE... PET FOOD AND FIRST AID SHOULD BE INCLUDED... A CANDLE FOR EACH PERSON, INSTEAD OF TWO CANDLES."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance and examples from a three-day shelter experiment: refrigeraton may not be available so adjust contents (substitute juices, etc.); the second day's menu should be the most substantial because morale tends to be lowest then; include pet food and first-aid supplies; use one candle per person rather than two; plan menus assuming no refrigeration; wipe dishes with damp paper towels when running water is unavailable; test food and living conditions in advance; schedule definite times for activities to combat boredom (e.g., set hours for meals, practice, coloring); togetherness and maintaining family routines (bedtime stories, games) are emphasized as key morale boosters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morale and household procedures during sheltering
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for family behavior during an extended shelter period: remain together to boost morale; establish routines and scheduled activities to overcome boredom; improvise sleeping/rest arrangements and hygiene without utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the report: move mattresses into a hall to sleep in cramped 'sardine' fashion; quiet children with stories; assign specific times for activities (e.g., 'two o'clock—parchesi time', 'three o'clock—piano practice'); accept lack of running water and adapt dishwashing methods; note emotional responses (children's comments) and plan accordingly. These procedural suggestions are presented as lessons learned from a real test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirement under the Subversive Activities Control Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal/administrative standard as applied by the Subversive Activities Control Board: organizations the Attorney General found to be Communist-front groups at the time of the Act's enactment must register; petitions may be dismissed if the organization no longer exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board dismissed a petition to require the American Slav Congress to register because the organization was found to be no longer in existence for purposes of the Act; an examiner recommended dismissal on grounds the organization was not in existence when the action was instituted. The board has previously ordered registration in other cases (e.g., Labor Youth League) and examiners have recommended registration in additional pending cases (e.g., Jefferson School). There was a dissent arguing testimony was inadequate and urging further hearing; another dissent emphasized a literal statutory reading that groups existing at the date of enactment should be registered. (Context: prior court-directed dismissals and differing examiner recommendations are cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Truce Commissions' proper role under the Geneva Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Normative standard stated by officials: the truce commissions' main job is to supervise the truce and investigate alleged violations, not to find a permanent solution to the Indochina crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: British Prime Minister Eden (as co‑chairman of the Geneva Conference) reportedly criticized commissions (under India's chairmanship) for focusing on finding a permanent solution rather than carrying out supervisory and investigatory functions; his letter to Nehru expressing this critique reportedly angered Nehru. This articulates an operational limitation on truce commissions' mandate under the Geneva framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational rules in the Jerusalem area armistice agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of an oral agreement between Israeli and Jordan commanders to prevent or suppress all firing in a specified rectangular sector around Jerusalem: limit forces to well‑trained, disciplined personnel and establish restraining orders on use of fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific provisions cited: the agreement applies to a rectangular stretch roughly six miles long by four miles wide centered on the Jerusalem railway station (covering New and Old Jerusalem environs); only well‑trained and disciplined military personnel and sentries are to be posted; explicit orders not to fire except in the case of danger of attack; establishment of direct telephone lines and procedures for reporting incidents; senior officers may be called by UN staff to settle disturbances; UN observers will take immediate action on any report of firing or hostile acts to stop such acts. The text also describes investigative and follow-up procedures (sending observers, using bloodhounds in a raid case) as operational practice under the agreement.
